fact: PPI describes pixel density in a digital image or display, while DPI traditionally describes printer dots on paper.
why: The terms are often used interchangeably, but pixels and printed ink dots are different units.
quizPrompt: Which abbreviation refers to pixels per inch?
quizAnswer: PPI.

fact: Your brain can perceive a complete shape even when parts of its outline are missing.
why: This Gestalt principle, called closure, lets incomplete logos, icons, and drawings remain recognizable.
quizPrompt: What Gestalt principle makes an incomplete outline look complete?
quizAnswer: Closure.

fact: Bearings to two or more known landmarks can locate you where the reverse bearing lines intersect on a map.
why: This navigation technique, called resection, converts visible landmarks into an estimated position.
quizPrompt: What is locating yourself from bearings to known landmarks called?
quizAnswer: Resection.

fact: Contour lines normally do not cross because one ground point cannot have two different elevations.
why: Crossing contours would imply conflicting heights at the same location; rare overhangs require special treatment.
quizPrompt: Why do contour lines normally never cross?
quizAnswer: A single ground point cannot have two elevations.

fact: A GPS receiver generally needs signals from at least four satellites for a three-dimensional position fix.
why: It solves for latitude, longitude, altitude, and the receiver clock's timing error at the same time.
quizPrompt: Why does a basic 3D GPS fix generally need four satellites rather than three?
quizAnswer: The fourth signal helps solve the receiver's clock error.

fact: The same latitude and longitude can indicate slightly different ground positions when different map datums are used.
why: A datum defines the reference model and alignment used to fit coordinates to Earth.
quizPrompt: What map setting can shift a coordinate even when its latitude and longitude numbers stay the same?
quizAnswer: The map datum.

fact: A whole number is divisible by 11 when the alternating sum of its digits is divisible by 11, including zero.
why: For 4,785, the alternating sum is 4 minus 7 plus 8 minus 5, which equals zero, so 4,785 is divisible by 11.
quizPrompt: Using the alternating-digit test, is 4,785 divisible by 11?
quizAnswer: Yes; its alternating sum is zero.

fact: Averaging two group averages is correct only when the groups have equal sizes.
why: With unequal groups, the combined average must weight each group by how many values it contains.
quizPrompt: When can two group averages be averaged directly?
quizAnswer: When the groups are the same size.

fact: Two successive 10 percent increases produce a total increase of 21 percent, not 20 percent.
why: The second increase applies to the already larger amount: 1.10 times 1.10 equals 1.21.
quizPrompt: What total increase results from two successive 10 percent increases?
quizAnswer: Twenty-one percent.

fact: A tightly coiled extension cord can overheat under a heavy electrical load more easily than the same cord laid out.
why: Coiling reduces the cord's exposed surface area and traps heat, so high-current tools should follow the cord maker's load and uncoiling guidance.
quizPrompt: Why can a loaded extension cord run hotter when tightly coiled?
quizAnswer: The coil traps heat and reduces cooling.

fact: A wrench's marked size usually describes the distance across the flat sides of the fastener head, not the bolt's thread diameter.
why: A bolt and the tool that turns its head can therefore carry different nominal measurements.
quizPrompt: What part of a hex fastener does a wrench size match?
quizAnswer: The distance across the flats of its head or nut.

fact: Crushing or finely chopping garlic usually creates a stronger flavor than leaving the clove whole.
why: Breaking more cells lets the enzyme alliinase form more pungent sulfur compounds, including allicin.
quizPrompt: Why is crushed garlic usually more pungent than a whole clove?
quizAnswer: More broken cells allow more pungent sulfur compounds to form.

fact: Bread often stales faster in a refrigerator than at room temperature, although freezing slows staling for longer storage.
why: Cool refrigerator temperatures speed starch retrogradation even while they discourage mold growth.
quizPrompt: For longer storage with less staling, is bread generally better refrigerated or frozen?
quizAnswer: Frozen.

fact: Clouds often look white because their droplets scatter many visible wavelengths of sunlight together.
why: Thick clouds can look gray when less light makes it through to their bases.
quizPrompt: Why do many sunlit clouds appear white?
quizAnswer: Their droplets scatter many visible wavelengths together.
